Genesis.author: Traditionally Moses
Genesis.date: Events from creation to c. 1805 BC
Genesis.theme: God creates a good world, humanity falls into sin, and God begins his rescue by calling Abraham and promising to bless all nations through his family.
outline: The fall, the flood and the nations
Genesis.christ: The promised offspring of the woman who will crush the serpent (3:15), the seed of Abraham in whom all nations are blessed.

Exodus.author: Traditionally Moses
Exodus.theme: God hears his enslaved people, redeems them from Egypt through the Passover and the sea, makes a covenant with them at Sinai, and comes to dwell among them in the tabernacle.
outline: Slavery and the call of Moses
Exodus.christ: The Passover lamb whose blood saves (1 Corinthians 5:7), and the tabernacle where God dwells with his people (John 1:14).

Leviticus.author: Traditionally Moses
Leviticus.theme: How a holy God can live among a sinful people: sacrifices, priests, clean and unclean, the Day of Atonement, and a call to be holy.
Leviticus.christ: The once-for-all sacrifice and great high priest that every offering pointed to (Hebrews 9–10).

Numbers.author: Traditionally Moses
Numbers.theme: Israel is counted, sets out from Sinai, refuses to enter the land in unbelief, and wanders until a new generation stands on the edge of the promise.
Numbers.christ: The bronze serpent lifted up so that those who look may live (John 3:14-15), and the rock that gave water (1 Corinthians 10:4).

Deuteronomy.author: Traditionally Moses
Deuteronomy.date: On the plains of Moab, c. 1406 BC
Deuteronomy.theme: Moses' farewell sermons: remember what God has done, love him with all your heart, and keep his covenant in the land.
outline: Laws for life in the land
Deuteronomy.christ: The prophet like Moses whom God would raise up (18:15; Acts 3:22); Jesus answered temptation from this book.

Joshua.author: Traditionally Joshua, with later additions
Joshua.theme: God keeps his promise: Israel crosses the Jordan, takes the land and receives its inheritance, and is called to serve the LORD alone.
Joshua.christ: Joshua (Hebrew Yeshua, the same name as Jesus) leads God's people into rest; the commander of the LORD's army (5:13-15).

Judges.author: Unknown; traditionally Samuel
Judges.theme: A downward cycle of sin, oppression, crying out and rescue by judges, in days when everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
outline: The judges: Deborah, Gideon, Jephthah, Samson…
Judges.christ: The flawed judges point to the true deliverer and king Israel needed.

Ruth.author: Unknown
Ruth.date: Set in the days of the judges
Ruth.theme: A Moabite widow's loyalty and a kinsman-redeemer's kindness: God's quiet providence brings a foreigner into the line of King David.
Ruth.christ: Boaz the kinsman-redeemer; Ruth is an ancestor of Jesus (Matthew 1:5).

1 Samuel.author: Unknown; draws on records of Samuel, Nathan and Gad
1 Samuel.theme: Israel moves from judges to kings: Samuel, the rise and failure of Saul, and God's choice of David, a man after his own heart.
1 Samuel.christ: The anointed king (messiah) chosen by God, and Hannah's song echoed in Mary's (Luke 1:46-55).

2 Samuel.author: Unknown
2 Samuel.theme: David's reign: his victories and God's everlasting covenant with his house, then his sin with Bathsheba and its costly consequences.
2 Samuel.christ: The son of David whose kingdom God promised to establish for ever (7:12-16; Luke 1:32-33).

1 Kings.author: Unknown; compiled during the exile
1 Kings.theme: Solomon's wisdom and temple, the kingdom split in two, and Elijah's stand for the LORD against Baal.
1 Kings.christ: One greater than Solomon (Matthew 12:42); the temple where God's glory dwelt.

2 Kings.author: Unknown; compiled during the exile
2 Kings.theme: Elisha's ministry, the fall of Israel to Assyria and of Judah to Babylon, because the people would not turn from idols.
2 Kings.christ: The line of David preserved even in exile (25:27-30), keeping the promise alive.

1 Chronicles.author: Traditionally Ezra
1 Chronicles.date: Written after the exile, c. 450–400 BC
1 Chronicles.theme: Israel's story retold for the returned exiles, centred on David, the ark and preparations for the temple.
1 Chronicles.christ: The everlasting throne of David's son (17:11-14).

2 Chronicles.author: Traditionally Ezra
2 Chronicles.theme: Solomon's temple and the kings of Judah: blessing when they sought the LORD, ruin when they forsook him, ending with Cyrus' decree to rebuild.
outline: The kings of Judah, the exile and Cyrus' decree
2 Chronicles.christ: The true temple (John 2:19-21) and the king who will reign in righteousness.

Ezra.author: Traditionally Ezra
Ezra.theme: The exiles return, rebuild the temple despite opposition, and are renewed by God's word under Ezra the scribe.
outline: The return and the temple rebuilt
Ezra.christ: God keeps his people and his promises through exile, preparing for the Messiah's coming.

Nehemiah.author: Nehemiah (memoir), with Ezra
Nehemiah.theme: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls in 52 days through prayer and hard work, and the people renew the covenant.
Nehemiah.christ: A servant-leader who gives up comfort to restore God's city.

Esther.author: Unknown
Esther.theme: God, never named, works through a Jewish queen and her cousin to save his people from destruction; the origin of Purim.
Esther.christ: One who risks her life to intercede for her people before the king.

Job.author: Unknown
Job.date: Set in the patriarchal age; date of writing uncertain
Job.theme: A righteous man loses everything; his friends' tidy answers fail, and God answers from the whirlwind with himself.
Job.christ: The Redeemer who lives (19:25) and the mediator Job longed for (9:33).

Psalms.author: David (73 psalms), Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses and others
Psalms.theme: Israel's prayer book and hymnbook: praise, lament, thanksgiving, trust and confession, gathered into five books.
Psalms.christ: The most quoted book in the New Testament: the anointed king (2), the suffering one (22), the priest-king (110).

Proverbs.author: Mainly Solomon, also Agur and Lemuel
Proverbs.theme: Wisdom for everyday life, beginning with the fear of the LORD: words, work, money, friendship and family.
outline: Agur, Lemuel and the woman of worth
Proverbs.christ: The wisdom of God made flesh (1 Corinthians 1:24, 30; compare Proverbs 8).

Ecclesiastes.author: “The Preacher,” traditionally Solomon
Ecclesiastes.theme: Life under the sun is vapour and cannot satisfy; so fear God, keep his commandments, and enjoy his gifts with gratitude.
Ecclesiastes.christ: The one Shepherd who gives meaning (12:11) and life beyond the sun.

Song of Solomon.author: Traditionally Solomon
Song of Solomon.theme: A love song celebrating the delight and faithfulness of love between a bride and her beloved.
Song of Solomon.christ: Read for centuries as a picture of the love between Christ and his church (Ephesians 5:25-32).

Isaiah.author: Isaiah son of Amoz
Isaiah.theme: The Holy One of Israel judges his people and the nations, then comforts them with promises of a coming King, a suffering Servant and new creation.
outline: Comfort: the Servant of the LORD
Isaiah.christ: Immanuel born of a virgin (7:14), the child-king (9:6), the suffering Servant (53).

Jeremiah.author: Jeremiah, with his scribe Baruch
Jeremiah.theme: The weeping prophet warns Judah for forty years, sees Jerusalem fall, and promises a new covenant written on the heart.
Jeremiah.christ: The righteous Branch of David (23:5-6) and the new covenant in his blood (Luke 22:20).

Lamentations.author: Traditionally Jeremiah
Lamentations.theme: Five poems of grief over fallen Jerusalem, with hope at the centre: his mercies are new every morning.
Lamentations.christ: The one who wept over Jerusalem (Luke 19:41) and bore God's wrath for his people.

Ezekiel.author: Ezekiel, a priest in exile
Ezekiel.theme: Visions of God's glory leaving the temple and returning; judgement on Jerusalem, a new heart and spirit, dry bones raised, and a new temple.
outline: Restoration: the good shepherd, dry bones
Ezekiel.christ: The true shepherd from David's line (34:23), and the river of life flowing from God's house (47; John 7:38).

Daniel.author: Daniel
Daniel.theme: Faithfulness in Babylon and the God who rules the kingdoms of men, revealed through stories and visions of empires and the kingdom that will never end.
outline: Daniel and his friends in Babylon
Visions of the kingdoms and the end
Daniel.christ: The Son of Man coming with the clouds to receive an everlasting kingdom (7:13-14) — Jesus' favourite title for himself.

Hosea.author: Hosea
Hosea.theme: Hosea's marriage to unfaithful Gomer pictures God's relentless love for unfaithful Israel.
Hosea.christ: Called out of Egypt (11:1; Matthew 2:15); the husband who buys back his bride.

Joel.author: Joel
Joel.theme: A locust plague foreshadows the Day of the LORD; return with all your heart, and God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh.
outline: Return to the LORD; the Spirit promised
Joel.christ: Fulfilled at Pentecost (Acts 2:16-21): everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

Amos.author: Amos, a shepherd of Tekoa
Amos.theme: A country prophet confronts prosperous Israel's injustice and empty worship: let justice roll down like waters.
outline: Five visions; restoration of David's tent
Amos.christ: The fallen tent of David rebuilt so that the nations may seek the Lord (9:11-12; Acts 15:16-17).

Obadiah.author: Obadiah
Obadiah.theme: Edom's pride and cruelty to Judah will be judged; the kingdom will be the LORD's.
Obadiah.christ: The kingdom shall be the LORD's (v. 21).

Jonah.author: Unknown; about Jonah son of Amittai
Jonah.theme: A reluctant prophet runs from God, is swallowed and spared, and resents God's mercy to Nineveh.
Jonah.christ: The sign of Jonah: three days and nights, then resurrection (Matthew 12:40).

Micah.author: Micah of Moresheth
Micah.theme: Judgement on corrupt leaders and hope in a ruler from Bethlehem; what the LORD requires: justice, kindness and humility.
outline: The LORD's case and his pardon
Micah.christ: Born in Bethlehem, whose origins are from of old (5:2; Matthew 2:6).

Nahum.author: Nahum
Nahum.theme: The fall of Nineveh: the LORD is slow to anger but will not leave the guilty unpunished, and is a refuge for those who trust him.
Nahum.christ: The feet of one bringing good news, proclaiming peace (1:15).

Habakkuk.author: Habakkuk
Habakkuk.theme: A prophet wrestles with God over evil and Babylon's coming, and learns to live by faith and rejoice in God even with empty fields.
outline: God's answer: the righteous live by faith
Habakkuk.christ: The righteous shall live by faith (2:4; Romans 1:17).

Zephaniah.author: Zephaniah
Zephaniah.theme: The great Day of the LORD will sweep the earth, then God will gather a humble remnant and rejoice over them with singing.
Zephaniah.christ: The King of Israel, the LORD, in your midst (3:15).

Haggai.author: Haggai
Haggai.theme: The returned exiles are told to stop building their own houses and rebuild God's; the latter glory will be greater.
outline: The coming glory; Zerubbabel the signet
Haggai.christ: The desire of all nations filling the house with glory (2:7-9).

Zechariah.author: Zechariah
Zechariah.theme: Night visions and oracles encourage the temple builders and look ahead to the coming King and the LORD's reign over all the earth.
outline: The coming King and the Day of the LORD
Zechariah.christ: The humble king on a donkey (9:9), sold for thirty pieces of silver (11:12-13), the pierced one (12:10).

Malachi.author: Malachi
Malachi.theme: God's love questioned, careless worship and broken faith rebuked; the messenger and the Sun of righteousness promised.
outline: The Day of the LORD and Elijah
Malachi.christ: Prepared for by the messenger, John the Baptist (3:1; 4:5; Matthew 11:10-14).

Matthew.author: Matthew (Levi), the tax collector and apostle
Matthew.theme: Jesus is the Messiah, the son of David and of Abraham, who fulfils the Scriptures and teaches the way of the kingdom of heaven.
outline: The kingdom in word and deed
Matthew.christ: The King of the Jews, Immanuel — God with us.

Mark.author: John Mark, drawing on Peter's preaching
Mark.theme: Fast-moving and vivid: Jesus the Son of God comes not to be served but to serve and give his life as a ransom.
Mark.christ: The servant Son of God, confessed at the cross by a Roman soldier (15:39).

Luke.author: Luke, the physician and companion of Paul
Luke.theme: An orderly account of Jesus the Saviour of the world, who seeks the lost, the poor and the outsider.
Luke.christ: The Son of Man who came to seek and save the lost.

John.author: John, the beloved disciple
John.theme: Seven signs and seven “I am” sayings, written so that you may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
John.christ: The eternal Word, God the Son, the bread of life, the light of the world, the resurrection and the life.

Acts.author: Luke
Acts.theme: The risen Jesus pours out his Spirit, and the good news spreads from Jerusalem to Judea and Samaria and to the ends of the earth.
outline: Paul's arrest and journey to Rome
Acts.christ: The ascended Lord, still working through his Spirit and his church.

Romans.author: Paul
Romans.theme: The gospel is the power of God for salvation: all have sinned, all may be justified by faith, and the justified live a new life by the Spirit.
Romans.christ: Set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood (3:25).

1 Corinthians.author: Paul
1 Corinthians.theme: Paul corrects a gifted but divided church: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, idol food, worship, spiritual gifts — and love, and the resurrection.
outline: Divisions and the wisdom of the cross
1 Corinthians.christ: Christ crucified, the power and wisdom of God; the firstfruits of the resurrection.

2 Corinthians.author: Paul
2 Corinthians.theme: Paul's most personal letter: ministry in weakness, the new covenant, the generosity of grace, and power made perfect in weakness.
2 Corinthians.christ: He who knew no sin became sin for us (5:21); though rich, he became poor (8:9).

Galatians.author: Paul
Galatians.theme: No other gospel: we are justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law, and called to freedom in the Spirit.
outline: Freedom and the fruit of the Spirit
Galatians.christ: Who loved me and gave himself for me (2:20); redeemed us from the curse (3:13).

Ephesians.author: Paul, from prison
Ephesians.theme: Every spiritual blessing in Christ: saved by grace, Jew and Gentile one body, and called to walk worthy, filled with the Spirit and armed for the fight.
Ephesians.christ: Head over all things for the church, which is his body (1:22-23).

Philippians.author: Paul, from prison
Philippians.theme: A joyful thank-you letter: to live is Christ, have his humble mind, press on, and rejoice in the Lord always.
Philippians.christ: He emptied himself, became obedient to death on a cross, and was highly exalted (2:5-11).

Colossians.author: Paul, from prison
Colossians.theme: Christ is supreme over creation and the church; in him the fullness of God dwells, so set your minds on things above.
Colossians.christ: The image of the invisible God, firstborn of all creation, in whom all things hold together.

1 Thessalonians.author: Paul
1 Thessalonians.theme: Encouragement to a young persecuted church: grow in holiness and love, and do not grieve without hope, for the Lord will come.
1 Thessalonians.christ: Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come (1:10).

2 Thessalonians.author: Paul
2 Thessalonians.theme: Stand firm: the Day of the Lord has not already come; until then, keep working and do not grow weary in doing good.
2 Thessalonians.christ: The Lord Jesus revealed from heaven in glory (1:7).

1 Timothy.author: Paul
1 Timothy.theme: Instructions to Timothy at Ephesus: sound teaching, prayer, leaders who are above reproach, and godliness with contentment.
1 Timothy.christ: The one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus (2:5).

2 Timothy.author: Paul, awaiting execution in Rome
2 Timothy.theme: Paul's last letter: guard the gospel, endure hardship, hold to the Scriptures, preach the word; I have kept the faith.
outline: Do not be ashamed; be strong
2 Timothy.christ: Who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light (1:10).

Titus.author: Paul
Titus.theme: Put the churches of Crete in order: appoint elders, teach sound doctrine, and let grace train believers for good works.
Titus.christ: Our great God and Saviour, who gave himself to redeem us (2:13-14).

Philemon.author: Paul, from prison
Philemon.theme: A personal appeal to receive back the runaway slave Onesimus — now a brother in Christ.
Philemon.christ: Paul offers to pay Onesimus' debt — a picture of Christ's substitution (v. 18).

Hebrews.author: Unknown
Hebrews.theme: Jesus is better: better than angels, Moses and the priests; the great high priest of a better covenant and a once-for-all sacrifice. So hold fast and run with endurance.
Hebrews.christ: The radiance of God's glory, our great high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

James.author: James, the brother of Jesus
James.theme: Real faith works: joy in trials, doers of the word, no favouritism, a tamed tongue, humility and patient prayer.
outline: Trials and doers of the word
James.christ: The Lord of glory (2:1), whose coming is near (5:8).

1 Peter.author: Peter
1 Peter.theme: Hope for suffering Christians scattered as exiles: a living hope, a holy people, and following Christ in suffering before glory.
outline: A living hope and a holy people
1 Peter.christ: He bore our sins in his body on the tree; by his wounds you were healed (2:24).

2 Peter.author: Peter
2 Peter.theme: Grow in grace and knowledge, beware false teachers, and look for the day of the Lord and the new heavens and earth.
2 Peter.christ: Seen in majesty on the holy mountain (1:16-18).

1 John.author: John
1 John.theme: So that you may know you have eternal life: walk in the light, love one another, and believe that Jesus came in the flesh.
1 John.christ: The Word of life, our advocate with the Father, the propitiation for our sins (2:1-2).

2 John.author: John, “the elder”
2 John.theme: Walk in truth and love, and do not welcome teachers who deny that Jesus came in the flesh.
2 John.christ: Jesus Christ come in the flesh (v. 7).

3 John.author: John, “the elder”
3 John.theme: Praise for Gaius' hospitality to travelling teachers, and a warning about proud Diotrephes.
3 John.christ: For the sake of the Name they went out (v. 7).

Jude.author: Jude, brother of James and of Jesus
Jude.theme: Contend for the faith once delivered, beware ungodly intruders, and keep yourselves in God's love — he is able to keep you from falling.
Jude.christ: Our only Master and Lord (v. 4), who is able to keep us.

Revelation.author: John, exiled on Patmos
Revelation.theme: The risen Christ speaks to seven churches; the Lamb opens the scroll of history; evil is judged, and God makes all things new.
outline: The new heaven and new earth
Revelation.christ: The Alpha and Omega, the Lamb who was slain, King of kings and Lord of lords.
